transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yes, thank you. Um, well, things have just been really... off lately. I work as a teaching assistant over at the university—mostly for the undergrad literature seminars. I actually have my master's, but I'm helping with the freshman classes right now. We're doing Victorian lit, which usually I love. I spent all weekend grading these essays on *Great Expectations*, and honestly, half of them clearly just read the SparkNotes. It’s so frustrating when you put so much effort into the syllabus, you know? My husband always says I care way too much about it and I should just give them their B-minuses and move on. 

But anyway, um, what I was saying... what really scares me, and why I made the appointment, is that lately when I walk across campus to get to the lecture hall, it feels... it feels like I’m watching everything through a pane of glass. Like I’m not fully in my own body? And the brick buildings and all the students around me just seem slightly unreal. Like I'm floating past a movie set. Which reminds me, they were actually filming a movie near the campus library last month, they had all these huge lights set up and completely redirected the foot traffic, made me late for my own section... but yeah, I just feel totally unreal and disconnected when I'm walking around.
When you say you feel like you’re not fully in your own body, do you also feel detached from yourself — like you're observing your own thoughts or actions from outside?

Yeah, exactly. Like I was just saying with the pane of glass thing... it's exactly like that. I feel like I'm sitting somewhere behind my own eyes, just watching myself do things. I'll be walking past the bell tower, and the buildings still look completely fake and unreal, but I'll also realize I'm just sort of... watching myself walk. 

Or I'll look down at my hands holding a red pen while I'm grading and think, 'Whose hands are those?' Which is ridiculous because I've been using the exact same brand of red pens for years. I used to buy them in bulk from this little independent stationery shop downtown. Actually, they closed last month, which is an absolute tragedy. It feels like every cute local store is turning into a corporate coffee chain or a bank nowadays, you know? My husband and I used to get our anniversary cards there, they had this beautiful letterpress section. 

But um, what were we... right, the detachment. Yes. It's like I'm a passenger in my own head, just observing my own actions while everything around me feels like a weird simulation.

latest_inference.note: This turn confirms both depersonalization (F44.1) and derealization (F44.2) experiences as central symptoms. The patient describes feeling detached from themselves ('watching myself walk,' 'passenger in my own head') and from the environment ('everything around me feels like a weird simulation,' 'buildings... seem slightly unreal'). Other disorders from the previous list (F43.1, F32.0, F32.1, F33.0, F33.1) are ruled out due to absence of significant anxiety or depressive symptoms as primary complaints.
